title: Generative Imputation with Multi-level Causal Consistency for Variable Subset Forecasting

problem.claim: Variable Subset Forecasting becomes difficult when entire variables are unavailable during inference.

gap.claim: Correlation-based imputation fails in VSF because missing variables invalidate dependency learning and temporal covariate shift destabilizes learned correlation patterns.

contributions.claim: GIMCC performs causality-driven imputation for Variable Subset Forecasting.
The method enforces global causal isomorphism and local causal subgraph alignment through dual consistency constraints.
GIMCC uses multivariate spectral convolutions to preserve causal relationships while decoupling causality from spurious correlations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across five real-world domains report average MAE/RMSE improvements of 20–60% over correlation-based imputation baselines.
The authors report that GIMCC outperforms full-variable training, identified as Oracle, under temporal covariate shift.
The authors state that the work offers theoretically grounded guarantees for real-world deployment.

narrative_sequence.summary: VSF removes entire variables during inference, creating a forecasting challenge.
Existing correlation-based imputation is undermined by missing-variable collapse and temporal covariate shift.
GIMCC addresses the problem with causality-driven imputation and dual causal consistency constraints.
The method separates causal structure from spurious correlations and preserves causal relationships with multivariate spectral convolutions.
Experiments across five real-world domains report improvements over correlation-based baselines and Oracle under temporal covariate shift.

source_observation.claim: Correlation-based dependency learning becomes unreliable when variables are entirely missing or when temporal distributions shift.

interpretation.claim: Robust forecasting under variable absence may require structural signals that remain stable across missingness patterns and distribution changes.

application.claim: For forecasting systems exposed to changing variable availability, consider causal or otherwise invariant structural constraints alongside correlation-based modeling.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when causal constraints outperform correlation-based methods outside the reported VSF and temporal covariate shift settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five domains, datasets, forecasting horizons, or missing-variable patterns.
The abstract does not describe how the ground-truth causal graph is obtained or whether it is required at deployment.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical guarantees, baselines, statistical variation, or significance testing.
